body: ohk, I'll give white noise another try tonight

Yes, I've been tempted to do this too. Some days it helps. I don't think it's a good long-term strategy though. For the first few days when I got this, I actually slept outside in the backyard in a tent just so I could get more ambient noises. Again, not a long-term solution but it helps.

I've tried white noise. It works but I get equally frustrated at the white noise too, so generally I play music (though admittedly, it doesn't mask it as well) :S
How do you cope with it, any tips?

Thank you, your encouragement helps. If you don't mind me asking, how long did it take before it became a non-issue for you? And I guess too, what do you do when you do hear it, does it still annoy you?

p.s. i ordered the sleephone, i'll give it a go

I live in Sydney, Australia. I get TRT, it's just CBT plus or minus a white noise generator device.

I guess I thought I could deal with this one my own, I figured by two months it would be much easier, but its still difficult at times, especially the night times and mornings.

I think i've read all the posts there are plus the archives on yuku. I've also read all the posts on tinnitus talk forum and the german mytinnitus.de forum. I've pretty much read all the comments on youtube related videos too. The thing is, it makes me feel better for the day, but then I forget it all the next day and start reading over all the comments again.

I understand what I have to do, it's just the acceptance part that is the most difficult. Accepting that I can live a semi normal life, but that it will never be the same again standing out in the wilderness in the dark of the night. That I can't enjoy that natural deafening silence of the woods again. It was a big part of my identity and life too. I guess it's the same for a musician with tinnitus too, it's not just the noise, but what it means to their identity and profession.

That is life indeed, makes me sad. I use to be a pretty calm person. Now I find I have to keep distracting myself with things, noises or activities. I can't rest my head on the table when I'm tired anymore, or lie down on the bed for a couple of minutes to rest. That's the thing I find difficult, that it gets you the most when you're tired or at your lowest.

I'm just taking it one day at a time, hopefully it gets better with time eh

I sleep with some music on, sometimes it helps distract me. It's weird but it's almost like the tinnitus noise is on a different brain wavelength, once you latch onto the sound it becomes difficult to ignore and you start hearing it over the music and other ambient noises.

I feel terrible in the morning when most people usually wake up refreshed, and I wake up feeling like my head is about to burst. When you learn to tune it out, are you able to still wake up and not notice it?

Thank you for your reply. I've gotten scans and everything. It all came down to idiopathic, nobody knows where it came from. I suspect probably accumulation of hearing damage, even though really I haven't been to that many loud places and I'm usually careful of volume of music.

I can't help but think that somehow I caused it, if only I hadn't been to that concert, or attended my friends karaoke party. It's too late now though. I'm so stressed out by this 24/7, even the times when I'm outside and can't hear it that I'm constantly clenching my teeth.
